title: The popular version. Apollo's software lived on a chip.
description:
Apollo's software lived on a chip. It lived in wire. Core rope memory stored the program by weaving wires through and around magnetic cores.

A wire through a core meant a 1. A wire around it meant a 0. The software was physically woven into the memory.

The size of the Apollo Guidance Computer's fixed memory, in six modules. Each word was 16 bits, 15 of data and one for parity.

Women at Raytheon in Waltham, Massachusetts. Many were hired from the textile industry for their sewing skills. Others came from the Waltham Watch Company.

About eight weeks and $15,000 for each module. Those are the figures given in a detailed technical write up.

Once it was woven, the program could not be edited.

Sources:
- https://righto.com/2019/07/software-woven-into-wire-core-rope-and.html (read): fixed core rope memory held 36,864 words in six modules; erasable memory 2,048 words; 16-bit words (15 data bits plus parity); a 1 is stored by threading a wire through a core and a 0 by bypassing it; ropes wired by women at Raytheon in Waltham, Massachusetts, many hired from the textile industry for sewing skills and others from the Waltham Watch Company; nicknamed "LOL memory" for Little Old Ladies, a name the article says overlooks women of colour who also worked on it; about 8 weeks and $15,000 per module.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Guidance_Computer (read): fixed memory 36,864 words implemented as core rope; 2,048 words of erasable core memory; 16-bit word with 15 data bits and one parity bit; core rope made by weaving wires through and around magnetic cores; read-only and holds most of the AGC software.
